correctness.rationale: In the absorbing-zero semigroup, two positive paths commute exactly when neither endpoint match permits concatenation: two nonzero reverse products would give a cycle. A stationary idempotent conflicts exactly with positive paths incident to its vertex. Any maximal commutative subsemigroup has zero; its positive sources S and targets T are disjoint. Saturation adds all positive paths from S to T and every stationary path outside their support, preserving closure (all positive products are zero). Per-vertex support is necessary and sufficient: a missing path either has a neutral endpoint, starts in T or ends in S, or was already included; a missing idempotent conflicts with a path at that vertex. This proves uniqueness and the size polynomial, including isolated vertices and parallel paths. For p:u→v the incompatible paths ending at u and starting at v are disjoint by acyclicity; for e_v remove the stationary path from each endpoint count. On the line, admissibility requires first active letter S and last T; counting words with fixed first and last positions gives (3ⁿ−2n−1)/4 before including the diagonal. The bound on sizes uses floor(m²/4)−m nondecreasing for m≥2, attained by a balanced cut when comparing with the diagonal; n=1 has only the diagonal. If L=n(n+1)/2, summing centralizer deficits on the line gives (L+1)²−n(n−1)−2Σ_i i(n−i)=(L+1)²−n(n−1)(n+4)/3, equivalent to the claimed formula. The remark about reversing words is unnecessary; reversal alone does not preserve admissibility. From /workspace, python3 reproductions/algebra.py semigroup independently reproduced ordered pair totals from multiplication for lines n=1–12 (first five 4,12,35,89,196) and maximal clique counts and sizes for n=1–5. The inspected frozen checker reports 79 cases with explicit paths; it was not executed in this review. Finite tests do not establish the uniform proof or extend it to cyclic quivers.

value.rationale: It classifies maximal commutative subsemigroups of a natural zero semigroup and separates two intrinsic invariants: family counts see only reachability, but family sizes see the number of distinct paths. The complete size distribution and element-centralizer counts answer more than a single small-case size calculation; the line formula demonstrates the resulting count on a standard example. The local mechanism is elementary, but the fully specified cut support and weighted census are useful structural information.
